While primarily a molecular/biomarker study, it includes patients receiving hyperthermia as part of multimodal therapy. May provide relevant data on hyperthermia response. Needs full-text review to determine if this qualifies as phase II/III RCT data.

This is a diagnostic accuracy study assessing MRI performance for predicting tumour stage and circumferential resection margin in rectal cancer. The study involved 76 patients who underwent preoperative MRI assessment, with findings compared to histological results. There is no randomization, no intervention comparison, and no control group. This is an observational diagnostic study, not a randomised controlled trial.

This is explicitly described as 'a retrospective review of 325 patients' analyzing whether radial resection margin involvement predicts local recurrence or distant metastases. The study is observational and retrospective in nature, with no randomization or intervention assignment. It examines prognostic factors rather than testing an intervention in a controlled trial setting.

Based on the title and truncated abstract, this appears to be a review or discussion article about endorectal imaging techniques for staging rectal carcinoma. The abstract mentions 'numerous studies have demonstrated' suggesting it reviews existing literature rather than presenting original trial data. There is no indication of randomization, intervention, or controlled trial design.

This is an observational study of 75 patients who underwent planned reoperations after initial curative surgery for rectal cancer. The study analyzes patterns of tumor failure (local, regional, distant) and correlates them with anatomical and pathological factors. There is no randomization, no intervention being tested, and no control group. This is a retrospective clinicopathologic correlation study.

This is a multicenter randomized controlled trial with 1861 patients randomly assigned to either preoperative radiotherapy (5 Gy × 5 days) followed by total mesorectal excision OR total mesorectal excision alone. The study clearly states 'We conducted a multicenter, randomized trial' and describes random assignment to two treatment groups. With 1861 patients and multiple centers, this is consistent with a Phase III trial design. The study meets the selection criteria as a randomised controlled trial.

This is a randomised controlled trial with 204 patients randomly assigned to postoperative radiation alone OR radiation plus fluorouracil chemotherapy with systemic therapy. The abstract clearly states patients 'were randomly assigned' to two treatment arms. The study compares adjuvant therapy regimens in high-risk rectal carcinoma patients. While the exact phase is not explicitly stated, the design (randomized comparison of treatment regimens) and publication in NEJM suggest this is a Phase II or III trial. The study meets the selection criteria as a randomised controlled trial.
